newsitem.title: UK: UK's Hogg, farmers leader clash on green rates.
newsitem.headline: UK's Hogg, farmers leader clash on green rates.

text.p: UK farm minister Douglas Hogg and farmers' union leader Sir David Naish clashed on Thursday over the issue of compensation to farmers for the income losses caused by green rate revaluations.
UK farmers will have to show that compensation is justified, Hogg told the National Farmers Union on Wednesday.
"There are powerful arguments for not paying," Hogg told delegates at the NFU's annual general meeting. "The onus is on the farming industry to prove that I should."
The NFU's Naish attacked Hogg's reluctance to pay.
"Agriculture ministers elsewhere in Europe have all accepted compensation, and he hasn't," Naish said, speaking to reporters after Hogg's speech. "Why treat your farmers differently?"

The strength of sterling against other European currencies has meant the revaluation of sterling's green rate, used to convert agricultural subsidies and support prices set in ecu into the national currency. The effect is to cut the sterling value of payments to farmers.
EU farm policy allows moves to offset the effect.
Green rates can be partially frozen to mitigate the loss and Hogg told the delegates that he had pressed the EU commission for such a freeze.
The freeze would cover the rate used for arable aid payments as well as sheep and beef premia, he said. It would be worth 200 million stg to UK farmers over two years.
The other possibility is the payment of direct compensation to farmers for the effects of the revaluation. It would have to be 50 per cent financed by the UK.
Hogg had told EU farm commissioner Franz Fischler that it would be right to bring forward a compensation scheme, but that did not mean that the UK would be paying out under it, he told reporters.
